key_insight: Giving a language model read-only SQL access to structured perovskite device data raises quantitative question-answering accuracy to about 51%, versus 16–23% for standard passage retrieval.
engineering_relevance: Structured experimental databases can make AI literature assistants more useful for comparing solar-cell performance and answering aggregate materials questions.
method: Compute 755 ground-truth answers from measured device records.
Benchmark six retrieval architectures across 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers.
Equip an open 14B model with read-only SQL access on a single 24 GB GPU.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 45,441 device records; SQL-enabled accuracy reached 51.5% on historical literature and 50.8% on prospective literature.
watch_item: Accuracy remains near 51%, and deployment depends on reliable extraction and maintenance of structured experimental records.
paper_title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics
